column2: THE CROWD — the forums where ordinary users argue. Sweep reddit · hackernews · lobste.rs · dev.to · stackoverflow, collect EVERY thread address the sweep finds on this question, then run crowd.sh over ALL of them (not the first three) and count the people inside. Your number is the denominator of the whole fleet: how many separate humans said something, and what each side's share is.

THE RIVAL'S OWN HOUSE — the community of the side that is NOT ours, plus the vendors' own forums (r/codex, community.openai.com, the product's own Discourse/Discord-web, its subreddit). The most valuable sentence in any comparison is the one written by the other side's own users. Read the comments, not the announcements. A vendor's blog post is NOT evidence here.

THE CODE — what actually breaks in the open: GitHub issues, pull requests and repository READMEs; Stack Overflow questions; issue trackers. Search with 4-word token queries, not sentences. Report the issue numbers, their dates and their state.

THE MEASUREMENT — independent numbers: leaderboards, benchmark pages, papers (arxiv · crossref · openalex · europepmc), and any page that publishes a score. JavaScript pages are not an excuse: open them with the browser (`opencli browser <site> open/extract`), or say exactly which door failed. Report every number with its date and who produced it.

THE SPOKEN WORD — YouTube and Bilibili: find the videos where people TEST the subject, take their TRANSCRIPTS (`opencli youtube transcript`) and their COMMENTS. A transcript is the only place where someone narrates what actually happened over an hour of use.

THE ADVERSARY — you hunt the OPPOSITE of whatever the obvious answer is. Your queries are "why we moved off X", "switched back to Y", "X is overrated", "X production problems", "regret", "cancelled my subscription". If the crowd says A, your job is to bring the strongest case for B, with names and dates. Report the best counter-evidence you found, and say plainly if the counter-case is weak — that is also a finding.

THE OTHER LANGUAGES — zhihu · v2ex · linux-do · weibo · juejin · quora.de · Turkish and German forums. The non-English crowd often tests things nobody in English has written about yet. Translate the decisive quotes and keep the originals beside them.
